I · THE KNOTS

The explicit formula makes every zero a frequency: the primes are the chord the zeros sound together. So each zero is taken against the fundamental, and the ratio is approximated by the best whole-number ratio within the deck's own span of thirteen. That ratio is a torus knot. The remainder is the zero's comma, the part no two whole numbers can say. Because a best ratio in lowest terms is coprime, every knot here is a single strand: this spectrum never locks into rings. That is a property of the mapping, not a discovery about the zeros.

II · THE LEVELS

Each line is a zero, drawn at its own height. This is how the energy levels of a nucleus are drawn, and it is drawn that way here for a reason: the zeros repel one another with the same statistics as those levels. Notice the ladder crowding as it rises. The density of zeros at height t is log(t/2π)/2π, so the spectrum thickens for ever, slowly.

III · THE REPULSION

Divide each gap by the local mean gap and the spectrum becomes comparable at every height. Every curve below is drawn from its formula, never fitted.

IV · THE CHORD

The room's opening sentence, cashed. The silver staircase counts the primes with their powers, each step the logarithm of its prime: the raw count, from the sieve. The gold line never saw a prime. It is the smooth slope every count begins with, minus one wave for each zero above, summed: Riemann's explicit formula, computed here. Slide the chord fuller and the waves interfere into the very steps; slide it empty and the primes dissolve back into the slope. And the chord can be heard: each zero a partial at its own height, the formula's own weights for loudness. The scale is chosen, one anchor at A; the ratios and the weights are the zeros' own.
